Analysis of the three supplied npm archives (2026-10-24)

All three original SHA-256 values were verified. Original archives were scanned
with atomscan --no-update --analyze local --mode slow --follow=none -f json.
cleave facts was run on each full original path, and member call/flow facts
were inspected where needed. Complete raw reports, facts, decoded Lua, fetched
artifacts and .forage.json provenance are under scratch/triage-bad.

VERDICTS

@famir/database 0.0.9: BENIGN, disclosed offensive-tool component.
Entry index.js exports repositories, connector and manager. Registration uses
the application's dependency-injection container; creating the connector reads
DATABASE_CONNECTION_URL (default local Redis). connect() explicitly connects.
Repositories serialize caller-supplied campaign, donor/mirror target, lure,
redirector, session and HTTP-message objects into Redis. Message create()
base64-encodes request/response body buffers, serializes headers and other
fields, then calls the Redis stored-function interface; readFull reverses it.
Session secrets are generated using the common library's crypto randomBytes.
Session authorization, revocation and lure upgrade operate on stored campaign
state, rather than stealing a browser's existing session store.

redis-functions.js contains seven ordinary JS string literals, not an opaque
encoded payload. They were decoded as JSON string literals and all Lua
functions and Redis operations inspected: hash/set/sorted-set CRUD, expiry,
locking, indexing and counters. loadFunctions() explicitly flushes existing
functions and FUNCTION_LOADs the seven scripts; cleanup() explicitly FLUSHDBs
the configured DB. None of these paths starts a local shell, visits victim
sites, reads user credential files or activates an extra downloaded payload.
This is purposeful backend storage for a phishing/MITM platform, not evidence
of an npm installation compromise. The upstream README explicitly describes
phishing campaigns and a legitimate pentest/research purpose:
https://github.com/bitnoize/famir
That intended offensive purpose plausibly explains the external hostile label.
A deployment's authorization and actual intercepted traffic are unavailable;
the BENIGN verdict applies to this distributed library, not to an unknown
campaign that consumes it. Dangerous DB clearing and code-loading capabilities
remain notable. No package-name allowlist or suppression was introduced.

Referenced GitHub source and documentation were fetched using forager. Direct
runtime dependencies were recovered and inspected: @famir/domain 0.0.4,
@famir/common 0.0.8, @famir/http-tools 0.0.9, redis 6.2.1. First attempts at
common/domain 0.0.9 failed because those releases do not exist; registry data
established the actual current versions for the wildcard dependencies. Domain
exports models/tokens; common provides DI, errors, schemas, random generation,
base64 and AES-GCM/scrypt/zlib helpers; http-tools implements URL/header/body
parsing and mirror rewriting. These dependencies have no installation payload.
Wildcards and the absent lockfile prevent reconstructing a historical deployed
dependency graph. Current upstream source is context, not a reconstruction of
this original tarball. Phishing behavior in other Famir applications is not
attributed to this database archive.

@nx/node 23.3.0-beta.3: BENIGN developer scaffolding plugin.
Registry retrieval was byte-identical to the original. Main exports generators;
utils exports explicit waitForPortOpen/killPort utilities. Generators write
workspace projects, TS/config files, Docker configuration and test templates;
installation callbacks delegate to Nx's package-manager workflow. No lifecycle
install script exists in this package. CLI test execSync launches the generated
project and checks Hello World. Server templates GET the configured test server.
waitForPortOpen constructs a net.Socket, connects to options.host (default
localhost), resolves on connect, retries selected connection errors, and cleans
up the socket. killPort checks whether the port is used, calls kill-port, waits,
and checks again. The recovered kill-port implementation uses netstat/TaskKill
on Windows or lsof/kill on Unix, consistent with test-server cleanup.
vscode-debug-config reads existing launch configuration inspector ports and
writes a new --inspect setting. It does not probe its own running debugger.
These shell/socket/termination features and beta packaging are plausible
heuristic reasons for an external hostile label; its source provided no reason.

Direct declared dependencies at the specified versions or lower range bounds
were fetched and scanned: @nx/devkit, @nx/jest, @nx/js, @nx/eslint, @nx/docker
23.3.0-beta.3; tslib 2.3.0; semver 7.6.3; tcp-port-used 1.0.2; kill-port 1.6.1.
Relevant generator installation/entry paths and port utilities were inspected,
not just their scores. No unexpected install hook was found in these artifacts.
Referenced raw GitHub images and the application-proxy documentation were
fetched; they are SVG artwork/documentation, not executable acquisition stages.
Optional generator packages and a machine's final semver resolutions are not
pinned by this archive, so this is not an audit of every possible future install.

@tencentdb-agent-memory/memory-sdk-ts 1.0.0: BENIGN API SDK with unsafe TLS default.
Registry retrieval was byte-identical. Source and shipped JS match in behavior.
Imports only define/export classes. Constructor stores caller-provided endpoint,
API key and service ID. Public methods POST caller-supplied memory data to the
configured /v2 routes. readFile obtains temporary COS credentials from the
configured service, caches them with an expiry buffer, signs GETs with HMAC-SHA1,
restricts parsed storage hosts to Tencent COS public/internal forms, fetches text,
and retries a 403 once with refreshed credentials. It neither harvests local
credentials nor evaluates downloaded content. prepack/prepublishOnly build the
SDK; they are not consumer installation hooks. There are no declared runtime
dependencies. The optional require('undici') path configures an Agent with
rejectUnauthorized:false. Its catch path writes NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0;
in ordinary Node ESM require is absent, so this fallback is especially relevant.
That genuine process-wide security reduction remains SUSPICIOUS. Explicit
rejectUnauthorized:true bypasses this branch. Weak TLS defaults plausibly
explain the external hostile label, without establishing a covert attack.

A representative optional undici 6.21.3 was retrieved and its Agent dispatch
path inspected: connection options are forwarded to Client/Pool connectors.
It is not a pinned dependency of this SDK; installed optional contents are
unknown. The illustrative memory.tencentyun.com endpoint could not be fetched
(DNS failure); it is a documentation example and not a fixed runtime target.
Endpoint authority and application authorization remain deployment unknowns.

RULE CHANGES AND REGRESSIONS

- Relocated the request_body/response_body matcher from llm-proxy to HTTP
  message, retaining its matcher, platforms, file types, criticality and the
  LLM consumer reference. Generic body fields do not imply an LLM proxy.
- Renamed Redis client-key-vocabulary to redis-key-vocabulary with the same
  matcher, updating its objective consumer. Lua's redis.call/error_reply near
  keys does not establish a client object.
- Narrowed Node inspector checks to actual option-testing call syntax, retained
  HTML coverage, and kept the original consumer ID through a union. Added a
  separate notable inspector-option reference for launch configurations.
  Existing external-to-batch debug-tty-gated-exit.js and
  js-debugger-tty-gated-exit.js retain their suspicious evasion finding; the
  tty-aware CLI and dispersed subsystem controls acquire no suspicious finding.
- Added general Redis factory initialization, FUNCTION_LOAD, FUNCTION_FLUSH,
  embedded Lua registration and FLUSHDB coverage. Awaited method target names
  are absent from this build's symbol facts, so actual call-node matchers are
  used for the Redis methods. Comments and quoted call examples do not match.
- Added a notable actual require('kill-port') call observation, without claiming
  an imported module has already terminated a process.
- Replaced the Tencent domain atom's generic 'Regex component marker'
  description and baseline level with an accurate notable domain reference.
  Its matcher is unchanged. The engine now emits this atom in place of the
  redundant aggregate storage URL label in the SDK. No endpoint evidence is
  lost; an unrelated Tencent hostname alone would not prove object storage.

The focused check.py verifies real probes versus launch configurations, Redis
imports without calls, unrelated factory imports, comments versus API calls,
HTTP field co-occurrence without LLM context, and the retained LLM consumer.
It passed on saved post-change atomscan JSONL. Existing attack/benign regression
controls also passed. comparison.json records every changed archive member and
all root-level trait additions/removals. No hostile/suspicious attack coverage
was lost. The only removed independent behavior claim is Nx's false own-debugger
check, replaced by the accurate launch-option reference.

COUNTS AND CLASSIFIER

Counts are unique archive-root traits (not duplicate source/dist occurrences).
Famir: hostile 0 -> 0, suspicious 0 -> 0; notable 48 -> 53.
Nx: hostile 0 -> 0, suspicious 0 -> 0; notable 78 -> 79.
Memory SDK: hostile 0 -> 0, suspicious 1 -> 1; notable 76 -> 76.
The SDK's one suspicious ID occurs in both src/http.ts and dist/http.js.
The calibrated ML level remains -1 (below its classification grid) for all
three samples and their members, before and after. Raw root probabilities:
Famir .632245 -> .66450846; Nx .94399506 -> .9456977;
Memory SDK .929035 -> .929035. Raw probability is not the verdict threshold.
This model warns that its feature schema is v18 versus engine expectation v21;
new features need model retraining. This limitation was not used as evidence
of benign intent. Flow facts also report unresolved object/member flows;
manual source tracing supplies the behavior analysis instead of assuming those
flow gaps are a clean bill of health.

No MALICIOUS sample was established, so no hostile-trait quota was filled with
unsupported phishing, exfiltration, persistence or evasion assertions. External
hostile labels disagree with the artifact-level judgments for the reasons above.
The retained suspicious TLS behavior is compatible with a benign SDK verdict.

FINAL VALIDATION COMMAND: make validate

Nx Node 23.3.0-beta.3: scaffolding and tests; correct traits
Memory SDK 1.0.0: API client; retain unsafe TLS finding
